national_baseline: National baseline for Infiltration Trench (practice synthesis — not adopted regulation). Where design infiltration rate is specified (n=17), values cluster around 0.5 in/hr (range 0.01 in/hr–2.41 in/hr). Associated site water-quality depth (not practice-specific) in the same manuals (n=28) range 0.37 inches–1.61 inches (mode 1 inches) — site-wide sizing context, not a infiltration trench-only rule. Associated max drawdown / dewatering time in the same manuals (n=36) range 4 hours–120 hours (mode 72 hours) — site-wide sizing context, not a infiltration trench-only rule. Associated SHWT separation in the same manuals (n=31) range 12 inches–120 inches (mode 24 inches) — site-wide sizing context, not a infiltration trench-only rule. Use the controlling jurisdiction manual for project design. Prefer retention/runoff reduction where soils and groundwater allow.

regional_modifiers.title: Cold climate / freeze-thaw
regional_modifiers.text: Cold-climate manuals often adjust underdrain depth, planting, and winter maintenance for freeze-thaw. Verify frost-line and snowmelt criteria in the controlling manual.

regional_modifiers.title: Coastal / high water table
regional_modifiers.text: Coastal and high-water-table settings may reduce infiltration credit and require underdrains or impermeable liners. Use SHWT separation values from the matrix when present; otherwise defer to local criteria.

regional_modifiers.title: Karst / bedrock
regional_modifiers.text: Karst and shallow-bedrock settings often require lined facilities or prohibit untreated infiltration. Do not assume unlined infiltration from national defaults.

regional_modifiers.title: Arid / semi-arid
regional_modifiers.text: Arid-region manuals may use larger capture depths, different planting palettes, and tighter water budgets. Confirm media specs and irrigation constraints locally.

matrix_summary: Scoped to Tier A manuals only. 41 of 76 manuals mention practice_key=infiltration_trench (design_parameters.practice_mentions or BMP text). Numeric consensus uses mode/range of extracted values — not an adopted national standard. Statistics count only values whose supporting quote was found in the source manual and states the value (strict citation check).
